title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-23
content:
2026-03-23 - serving-runtime daily scratchpad (Ava)

Morning context:
- Focus: follow up on perf regression that showed up in canary yesterday (p99 latency spike on long-context chat workloads).
- Triage notes below include repro steps, quick measurements, and suspected kernel/caching interactions.
- Sync with Riley @ 11:30 to decide whether to roll back the canary or push a hotfix.

Quick summary:
- Regression surfaced in canary: p99 increased from ~420ms -> ~1.1s for requests with context length > 12k tokens. No increase on short sequences.
- Canary is using kernel build v2.4.1 + KV cache change (LRU tweak) landed in PR#4321 last week. Suspect interaction between new batching heuristic and KV cache eviction leading to cache miss storms for long prefixes.

Repro (local):
1) Checkout canary branch, start local runtime with --kernel=v2.4.1 --kv-cache=lru --batching=adaptive
2) Run bench script: tools/bench_long_context.sh --model redwood-open-70b --seq 12800 --qps 2 --concurrency 8
3) Observe tail latency histogram (prometheus exporter): p50 ~ 430ms, p95 ~ 600ms, p99 ~ 1.0-1.2s
4) Re-run with kernel v2.4.0 (previous): p99 ~ 430-480ms (back to expected).

Immediate hypothesis:
- The LRU eviction policy change inadvertently raises chance of evicting KV entries for very long prefix hits under adaptive batching. When a large request misses the cache, it triggers additional kernel work (KV reload + larger attention windows) causing queueing/backpressure and p99 spikes.
- Alternatively, a kernel scheduling regression in v2.4.1: some kernels (fused-attn) get scheduled differently for >8k seq and lead to longer compute times. Need microbench to isolate.

Data to collect (next 2 hours):
- Run repro with kv-cache=none (disabled) to see if p99 decreases. If yes -> cache eviction root cause.
- Run repro with adaptive batching disabled (fixed small batch size) to see effect.
- Profile kernel execution timeline for a single long request (trace spans + nvtx). Collect timeline and kernel durations.
- Export per-request cache hit/miss stats (prom exporter: runtime.kv_hits, runtime.kv_misses) and correlate with latency.

Short commands / notes:
- bench script: ./tools/bench_long_context.sh --model redwood-open-70b --seq 12800 --qps 2 --concurrency 8
- run local with old kernel: make dev-run KERNEL_TAG=v2.4.0 KV_CACHE=lru
- disable cache: make dev-run KV_CACHE=none
- profiling: ./tools/profile_request.sh --trace-id <id> --nvtx

Observations from quick runs (09:30):
- With KV_CACHE=none, p99 drops to ~520ms (better but still slightly higher than baseline). Suggests cache interactions are part of the issue but not the only cause.
- With adaptive batching disabled, p99 ~ 480ms (close to baseline). This strongly implicates the new batching heuristic interacting with KV behavior.

Next steps (prio order):
- [ ] Add temporary revert of the adaptive batching change in canary (hotfix) to mitigate while we root cause. (Riley to prepare revert PR)
- [ ] Instrument more detailed KV eviction logging (evict reason, eviction size, timestamp) to correlate with misses. (me)
- [ ] Microbench the new fused-attn scheduling for seq len thresholds to see if kernel cost changed in v2.4.1. (Ethan)
- [ ] Add a small dogfooding run in Dedicated region to confirm canary vs prod behaviour under real load. (Ops request)

Notes on kernel-level experiments:
- Try forcing non-fused attention kernel for seq > 8k to see if latency regresses or improves. Might be a fused kernel bug. Use env VAR KERNEL_FORCE_NO_FUSED_ATTENTION=1 in local dev-run.
- Check CUDA profiler traces for long memcpy operations between host/device (unlikely but check).

Bugs / tickets to update:
- JIRA-RT-789: "p99 spike on long-context canary after v2.4.1" -> add latest profiling output + bench logs.
- PR#4321: LRU tweak -> annotate with reproduction steps and request revert candidate.

Misc TODOs / personal reminders:
- Push small KV logging change by EOD. Keep log sampling low to avoid noise in prod.
- Follow up with Product (Sarah) re: whether we should temporarily reduce long-context canary traffic to reduce user impact if rollback delayed.
- Update runbook with new check: if p99 > 2x baseline, check KV miss rate and batching mode first.

Meeting notes (11:30 sync):
- Riley: will open revert PR for adaptive batching and tag QA. Suggested canary rollback if hotfix doesn't land quickly.
- Ethan: will share kernel profiling artifacts by 14:00.
- Decision: hold canary rollback until profiling confirms root cause, but prepare rollback PR ready to merge if user impact increases.

Follow-ups / longer-term improvements:
- Add synthetic long-context workload to daily perf regression suite (catch this earlier).
- Revisit adaptive batching algorithm: add guard rails for large-prefix scenarios (max batch size when avg prefix > X tokens).
- Consider KV cache aging policy that accounts for request prefix size to reduce odds of evicting high-value long-prefix entries.

Scratch/notes (random):
- Possible quick mitigation: if request.seq_len > 8k, route to dedicated small pool with conservative batching. Might be simplest short-term.
- Check telemetry: are specific customers hitting this? Filter by route/model and look at high seq_len requests.

End of notes. Will update after profiling results (14:00).

-- Ava
